Occupational Therapy Assistant Full-time

Award Care at Colonial Lakeshas an exciting opportunity for aFull-time Occupational Therapy Assistant (OTA)We are looking for a dedicated OTA to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.

AtAward Care at Colonial Lakes, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapy Assistant Responsibilities

  • Plan and administer occupational therapy treatments for residents and patients with temporary or long-term disabilities.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy services and interventions in accordance with physician orders and under the supervision of a licensed Occupational Therapist.
  • Respond to requests for occupational therapy services by communicating relevant information and making referrals to the Occupational Therapist as appropriate.
  • Ensure all treatment is provided in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Provide clinical support and education to patients, families, and caregivers.
  • Monitor and document patient responses to treatment interventions.
  • Complete all required documentation and forms in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy Assistant license inFL.
  • Current certification as a Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA).
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

Career Advantages

  • Full-time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

Laura Benoit

About Quality Rehab Management, LLC:

At QRM, we strive to make a difference in the lives of patients and in the operational success of the facilities and therapy teams we support. Our team is dedicated to empowering one another to achieve greatness and to creating lasting, meaningful change in the long-term care industry. Since our inception in 2018, we have seen our mission come to life, and we remain humbled and vigilant in our commitment to excellence. We understand collaboration is key when it comes to bolstering employee and client success. Through consistent education and enrichment, we can uncover new strategies which propel our clients towards success and strengthen our approach. By continuously keeping a watchful eye on the ever-changing nature of the long-term care industry, we remain alert and hold ourselves accountable for providing thoughtful support to our fellow team members who in turn provide excellent service to our clients.

Nexus at Elmwood Parkhas an exciting opportunity for aFull-time Occupational Therapy Assistant (OTA)inElmwood Park, ILWe are looking for a dedicated OTA to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.

AtNexus at Elmwood Park, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapy Assistant Responsibilities

  • Plan and administer occupational therapy treatments for residents and patients with temporary or long-term disabilities.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy services and interventions in accordance with physician orders and under the supervision of a licensed Occupational Therapist.
  • Respond to requests for occupational therapy services by communicating relevant information and making referrals to the Occupational Therapist as appropriate.
  • Ensure all treatment is provided in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Provide clinical support and education to patients, families, and caregivers.
  • Monitor and document patient responses to treatment interventions.
  • Complete all required documentation and forms in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy Assistant license inIL.
  • Current certification as a Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA).
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

Career Advantages

  • Full-time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

Caitlin Locke

About Quality Rehab Management, LLC:

At QRM, we strive to make a difference in the lives of patients and in the operational success of the facilities and therapy teams we support. Our team is dedicated to empowering one another to achieve greatness and to creating lasting, meaningful change in the long-term care industry. Since our inception in 2018, we have seen our mission come to life, and we remain humbled and vigilant in our commitment to excellence. We understand collaboration is key when it comes to bolstering employee and client success. Through consistent education and enrichment, we can uncover new strategies which propel our clients towards success and strengthen our approach. By continuously keeping a watchful eye on the ever-changing nature of the long-term care industry, we remain alert and hold ourselves accountable for providing thoughtful support to our fellow team members who in turn provide excellent service to our clients.

Aventura at Carriage Innhas an exciting opportunity for aFull-time Occupational Therapy Assistant (OTA)We are looking for a dedicated OTA to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.

AtAventura at Carriage Inn, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapy Assistant Responsibilities

  • Plan and administer occupational therapy treatments for residents and patients with temporary or long-term disabilities.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy services and interventions in accordance with physician orders and under the supervision of a licensed Occupational Therapist.
  • Respond to requests for occupational therapy services by communicating relevant information and making referrals to the Occupational Therapist as appropriate.
  • Ensure all treatment is provided in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Provide clinical support and education to patients, families, and caregivers.
  • Monitor and document patient responses to treatment interventions.
  • Complete all required documentation and forms in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy Assistant license inOH.
  • Current certification as a Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA).
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

Career Advantages

  • Full-time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

Caitlin Locke

About Quality Rehab Management, LLC:

At QRM, we strive to make a difference in the lives of patients and in the operational success of the facilities and therapy teams we support. Our team is dedicated to empowering one another to achieve greatness and to creating lasting, meaningful change in the long-term care industry. Since our inception in 2018, we have seen our mission come to life, and we remain humbled and vigilant in our commitment to excellence. We understand collaboration is key when it comes to bolstering employee and client success. Through consistent education and enrichment, we can uncover new strategies which propel our clients towards success and strengthen our approach. By continuously keeping a watchful eye on the ever-changing nature of the long-term care industry, we remain alert and hold ourselves accountable for providing thoughtful support to our fellow team members who in turn provide excellent service to our clients.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license inIL.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Career Advantages

  • Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license inIL.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

  • Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

Premier Nursing and Rehab Center of Far Rockaway has an exciting opportunity for a Occupational Therapist (OT)

We are looking for a dedicated OT to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.At Premier Nursing and Rehab Center of Far Rockaway, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license .
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Career Advantages

  • Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

At QRM, we strive to make a difference in the lives of patients and in the operational success of the facilities and therapy teams we support. Since our inception in 2018, we have seen our mission come to life, and we remain humbled and vigilant in our commitment to excellence. We understand collaboration is key when it comes to bolstering employee and client success. Through consistent education and enrichment, we can uncover new strategies which propel our clients towards success and strengthen our approach. Part-time/PRN Occupational Therapist (OT) - In-House Rehab Team

Cedar Rapids, IA

Position:Part-time or PRN

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

AtNorthbrook Manor Care Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time OT, you will be the driving force behind helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Evaluate & Treat:Develop and implement highly individualized care plans focused on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate:Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy and community integration.
  • Collaborate:Work hand-in-hand with our COTAs, PTs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate:Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document:Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education:Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.
  • Licensure:Active (or pending) state OT license in Iowa.
  • Certification:NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience:Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills:Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary:Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations:Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Culture:A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you

Part-time/PRN Occupational Therapist (OT) - In-House Rehab Team

Cedar Rapids, IA

Position:Part-time or PRN

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

AtNorthbrook Manor Care Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time OT, you will be the driving force behind helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Evaluate & Treat:Develop and implement highly individualized care plans focused on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate:Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy and community integration.
  • Collaborate:Work hand-in-hand with our COTAs, PTs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate:Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document:Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education:Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.
  • Licensure:Active (or pending) state OT license in Iowa.
  • Certification:NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience:Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills:Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary:Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations:Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Culture:A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you

Part-time/PRN Occupational Therapist (OT) - In-House Rehab Team

Cedar Rapids, IA

Position:Part-time or PRN

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

AtNorthbrook Manor Care Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time OT, you will be the driving force behind helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Evaluate & Treat:Develop and implement highly individualized care plans focused on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate:Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy and community integration.
  • Collaborate:Work hand-in-hand with our COTAs, PTs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate:Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document:Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education:Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.
  • Licensure:Active (or pending) state OT license in Iowa.
  • Certification:NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience:Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills:Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary:Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations:Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Culture:A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you

Fountain Care at Sunset Hillshas an exciting opportunity for aFull-time Occupational Therapist (OT)

NEW MANAGEMENT TEAM

We are looking for a dedicated OT to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.

AtFountain Care at Sunset Hills, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Career Advantages

  • Full-time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.

Premier Nursing and Rehab Center of Far Rockawayhas an exciting opportunity for aFull-time Occupational Therapist (OT)

We are looking for a dedicated OT to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.

AtPremier Nursing and Rehab Center of Far Rockaway, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license .
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Career Advantages

  • Full-time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

At QRM, we strive to make a difference in the lives of patients and in the operational success of the facilities and therapy teams we support. Since our inception in 2018, we have seen our mission come to life, and we remain humbled and vigilant in our commitment to excellence. We understand collaboration is key when it comes to bolstering employee and client success. Through consistent education and enrichment, we can uncover new strategies which propel our clients towards success and strengthen our approach. By continuously keeping a watchful eye on the ever-changing nature of the long-term care industry, we remain alert and hold ourselves accountable for providing thoughtful support to our fellow team members who in turn provide excellent service to our clients.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Physical Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive patient evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans using a variety of evidence-based physical therapy techniques and interventions.
  • Create personalized rehabilitation programs designed to help patients achieve their functional goals and maximize independence.
  • Administer medically prescribed physical therapy treatments to relieve pain, improve or restore function, increase mobility, and promote healing.
  • Ensure all treatment is provided in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team (IDT).
  • Provide clinical support, education, and guidance to patients, family members, and caregivers.
  • Collaborate with other members of the interdisciplinary team to promote coordinated, high-quality patient care.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Physical Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of physical therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with patients, families, caregivers, and members of the interdisciplinary team.

Part-time/PRN Physical Therapist (PT) - In-House Rehab Team

Cedar Rapids, IA

Position:Part-time or PRN

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

AtNorthbrook Manor Care Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time PT, you will lead the charge in restoring mobility, strength, and confidence for our residents.

  • Evaluate & Treat:Provide comprehensive functional assessments and design targeted, evidence-based treatment plans to address mobility, balance, gait, and pain management.
  • Innovate:Implement specialized programs (like fall prevention and joint replacement recovery) to ensure our patients achieve their highest possible level of independence and success.
  • Collaborate:Lead and partner seamlessly with our highly skilled Physical Therapist Assistants (PTAs), alongside OTs, SLPs, and nursing teams, to deliver cohesive clinical care.
  • Educate:Empower patients and their families with the physical tools and knowledge needed for safe discharges and active community integration.
  • Document:Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education:Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapy program (DPT preferred).
  • Licensure:Active (or pending) state PT license in Iowa.
  • Experience:Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills:Strong clinical reasoning, leadership capabilities, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary:Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations:Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Culture:A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you

Cedar Rapids, IA

Position:Part-time or PRN

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

AtNorthbrook Manor Care Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time PT, you will lead the charge in restoring mobility, strength, and confidence for our residents.

  • Evaluate & Treat:Provide comprehensive functional assessments and design targeted, evidence-based treatment plans to address mobility, balance, gait, and pain management.
  • Innovate:Implement specialized programs (like fall prevention and joint replacement recovery) to ensure our patients achieve their highest possible level of independence and success.
  • Collaborate:Lead and partner seamlessly with our highly skilled Physical Therapist Assistants (PTAs), alongside OTs, SLPs, and nursing teams, to deliver cohesive clinical care.
  • Educate:Empower patients and their families with the physical tools and knowledge needed for safe discharges and active community integration.
  • Document:Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education:Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapy program (DPT preferred).
  • Licensure:Active (or pending) state PT license in Iowa.
  • Experience:Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills:Strong clinical reasoning, leadership capabilities, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary:Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations:Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Culture:A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you

Cedar Rapids, IA

Position:Part-time or PRN

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

AtNorthbrook Manor Care Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time PT, you will lead the charge in restoring mobility, strength, and confidence for our residents.

  • Evaluate & Treat:Provide comprehensive functional assessments and design targeted, evidence-based treatment plans to address mobility, balance, gait, and pain management.
  • Innovate:Implement specialized programs (like fall prevention and joint replacement recovery) to ensure our patients achieve their highest possible level of independence and success.
  • Collaborate:Lead and partner seamlessly with our highly skilled Physical Therapist Assistants (PTAs), alongside OTs, SLPs, and nursing teams, to deliver cohesive clinical care.
  • Educate:Empower patients and their families with the physical tools and knowledge needed for safe discharges and active community integration.
  • Document:Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education:Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapy program (DPT preferred).
  • Licensure:Active (or pending) state PT license in Iowa.
  • Experience:Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills:Strong clinical reasoning, leadership capabilities, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary:Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations:Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Culture:A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Part-time/PRN Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) - In-House Rehab Team

Position:Part-time, PRN

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist Assistant who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Fairhaven, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time PTA, you will be on the front lines of restoring mobility, strength, and confidence for our residents.

  • Treat & Empower: Implement targeted, evidence-based treatment plans designed by the evaluating PT to address mobility, balance, gait, and pain management.
  • Innovate: Carry out specialized programs (like fall prevention and joint replacement recovery) to ensure our patients achieve their highest possible level of independence and success.
  • Collaborate: Partner seamlessly with our PTs, alongside COTAs, SLPs, and nursing teams, to deliver cohesive and comprehensive clinical care.
  • Educate: Empower patients and their families with the physical tools and knowledge needed for safe discharges and active community integration.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapist Assistant program.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state PTA license.
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is highly preferred, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical execution, empathy, adaptability, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your clinical insights as an assistant are truly valued.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you

Speech-Language Pathologist Responsibilities

  • Monitor progress and communicate changes in condition to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation and billing records in accordance with company policies and applicable requirements.
  • Respond to resident and family questions, requests, and concerns in a timely and professional manner.
  • Provide training and support to Restorative Nursing and other care staff.
  • Maintain resident and patient confidentiality and protect all personal health information.
  • Follow applicable federal, state, and local regulations, as well as professional standards and facility policies.
  • Attend required meetings and assist with other responsibilities as directed by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Speech-Language Pathologist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.
  • Knowledge of current speech-language pathology treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.

  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with residents and patients with a variety of needs, abilities, and personalities.

Summerford Health and Rehabhas an exciting opportunity for aFull-time Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP)to join our team

Full Time and Per Diem Needs

We're looking for a dedicated and compassionate SLP to join our in-house rehabilitation team and provide high-quality, person-centered care to our residents and patients. You'll have the opportunity to work alongside an experienced clinical team focused on helping each individual reach meaningful goals and maintain the highest level of independence possible.

AtSummerford Health and Rehab, our rehabilitation team valuescompassion, collaboration, and clinical excellence. We work together to create individualized treatment plans and provide care that meets the unique needs of each resident and patient.

If you're looking for a supportive team where your clinical expertise can make a real difference, we'd love to hear from you

Speech-Language Pathologist Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents and patients for speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing needs.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans focused on cognition, communication, swallowing, and functional independence.
  • Provide skilled, medically necessary speech-language pathology services in accordance with established plans of care.
  • Help residents and patients achieve their individualized cognitive, communication, and swallowing goals.
  • Provide education, training, and support for residents, families, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Collaborate with physicians and other healthcare professionals regarding diagnostic swallowing procedures, including Modified Barium Swallow Studies (MBSS) and Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES), as ordered and clinically indicated.
  • Apply sound clinical judgment and maintain skills consistent with current speech-language pathology standards of practice.
  • Monitor progress and communicate changes in condition to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation and billing records in accordance with company policies and applicable requirements.
  • Respond to resident and family questions, requests, and concerns in a timely and professional manner.
  • Provide training and support to Restorative Nursing and other care staff.
  • Maintain resident and patient confidentiality and protect all personal health information.
  • Follow applicable federal, state, and local regulations, as well as professional standards and facility policies.
  • Attend required meetings and assist with other responsibilities as directed by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Speech-Language Pathologist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.
  • Knowledge of current speech-language pathology treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with residents and patients with a variety of needs, abilities, and personalities.
  • Strong organization and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, and the interdisciplinary team.
  • A genuine commitment to compassionate, patient-centered care.

Speech-Language Pathologist Requirements

  • Active and valid Speech-Language Pathology license inAL.
  • Current ASHA certification.
  • Must be in good standing with applicable licensing boards and regulatory agencies.

Why Join Our Team?

  • Full-time opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates are welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive and collaborative clinical environment

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

Speech-Language Pathologist Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents and patients for speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing needs.

  • Provide skilled, medically necessary speech-language pathology services in accordance with established plans of care.
  • Help residents and patients achieve their individualized cognitive, communication, and swallowing goals.
  • Provide education, training, and support for residents, families, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Collaborate with physicians and other healthcare professionals regarding diagnostic swallowing procedures, including Modified Barium Swallow Studies (MBSS) and Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES), as ordered and clinically indicated.
  • Apply sound clinical judgment and maintain skills consistent with current speech-language pathology standards of practice.
  • Monitor progress and communicate changes in condition to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation and billing records in accordance with company policies and applicable requirements.
  • Respond to resident and family questions, requests, and concerns in a timely and professional manner.
  • Provide training and support to Restorative Nursing and other care staff.
  • Maintain resident and patient confidentiality and protect all personal health information.
  • Follow applicable federal, state, and local regulations, as well as professional standards and facility policies.
  • Attend required meetings and assist with other responsibilities as directed by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Speech-Language Pathologist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.
